summary: A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Bryan J. Cuevas studied at Emory University and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Princeton and later became John F. Priest Professor of Religion at Florida State University.

Bryan W. Van Norden is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Stanford University from around 1985 to 1991. Around 1996, he held a professorship at Vassar College in Philosophy and Chinese & Japanese.
Bryce Ryan worked in religious studies and related fields, teaching sociologist Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. Over his career, he held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon.

Bulcsu Siklós specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of London under doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski and teacher Charles Roskelly Bawden, and was later affiliated with SOAS University of London around 1996.

Bunkyo Aoki was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Ryukoku University and as a disciple of Kozui Otani (~1910–1914). In 1951, he succeeded Tokan Tada as a Tibetan language lecturer at the University of Tokyo.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Japanology, Bunsaku Kurata studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda Universities. He worked extensively with the National Commission for the Protection of Cultural Properties, served at the Tokyo National Museum, and became Director of Nara National Museum in 1975.

Bunyiu Nanjio was an indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He held key leadership posts at Otani University between 1895 and 1923 and taught at the University of Tokyo.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto was an indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as professor of Indian philosophy history and president (1908–1915) at Kyoto University, and later directed the Academy of Oriental Culture's Kyoto Institute.

Burchard Brentjes worked in archaeology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Heinz Adolf Mode at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1947 to 1952, held a post there (~1954–1976), and succeeded Mode in 1978.

Burkhard Quessel is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and was attested as a member there in 1997. He later served as a curator at the British Library, attested between 2002 and 2012.

Burton Stein was an historian and indologist. Over his career, he held academic appointments at the University of Hawaiʻi from around 1965 to 1989 and at SOAS University of London from around 1989 until 1996.

Burton Watson was a Sinologist and Japanologist who earned his BA and PhD at Columbia University, studying under William Theodore de Bary, and studied at Kyoto University. He held faculty posts at Columbia, Kyoto University, and Stanford University.

Byambyn Rinchen was a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Leningrad Orient Institute (~1924–1927) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1956–1957), and held a post at the National University of Mongolia.
Byung-gon Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied abroad at Rissho University (attested 2007). He serves as a professor, dean, and institute director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

C. D. Sebastian specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Banaras Hindu University, undertook postdoctoral study with Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa, and became Professor of Indian Philosophy at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay.

C. M. Naim is an indologist and linguist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1958 to 1960. He spent his career at the University of Chicago (~1961–2001), where he became Professor Emeritus.

C. Pierce Salguero specializes in Buddhist studies and the history of medicine, earning degrees from the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University. He has taught at Penn State Abington and served as editor-in-chief of Asian Medicine.
C. R. Krishnamacharlu was an Indologist and historian. He completed his education at Madras Christian College, earning an F.A., and earned a university degree from Pachaiyappa's College.

C. S. Srinivasachari was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held appointments as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University, where he is attested in 1932–1933.

C. Scott Littleton was a scholar of linguistics, Japanology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of California, Los Angeles from approximately 1955 to 1964, studying under Jaan Puhvel.
